title: NumPy: chained calls, views of an unnamed array, a 3-D slice
source:
import numpy as np

grid = np.arange(12).reshape(3, 4)
row = grid[1]
row[2] = -5
safe = grid.copy()
safe[0, 0] = 99
means = grid.mean(axis=0)
mask = grid > 5
print(grid[mask])
total = grid + np.array([10, 20, 30, 40])
cube = np.zeros((2, 2, 3))
cube[1] = 7

steps.narration: np.arange(12).reshape(3, 4) made a new 2-D ndarray of shape (3, 4), dtype int32: grid now refers to it.
grid[1] picks row 1 of grid, as a new array row of shape (4,).
Stored -5 in row[2]: index 2 of row (6 → -5).
Copied grid into a new ndarray safe with its own data: shape (3, 4).
Stored 99 in safe[0, 0]: the element at [0, 0] of safe (0 → 99).
Averaged grid along axis 0, down each column: one result per column, so shape (3, 4) becomes (4,).
Compared grid with 5 element by element using >: mask is a new bool ndarray of shape (3, 4).
grid + np.array([10, 20, 30, 40]) made a new 2-D ndarray of shape (3, 4), dtype int32: total now refers to it.
np.zeros((2, 2, 3)) made a 3-D ndarray filled with 0.0: shape (2, 2, 3), dtype float64. cube now refers to it.
Stored 7 in the slice [1, :, :] of cube.
